name: AML transaction monitoring
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Three layers of competition sit underneath AML transaction monitoring today and beava is closest to the bottom layer. (a) Generic streaming + feature-serving infrastructure under the incumbent AML platform: Apache Flink for stateful long-horizon counters (peer-group baselines over 90-365 days, structuring windows), Kafka Streams / ksqlDB for in-Kafka aggregation, Redis Enterprise / Cluster (now competing with Apache-2.0 Valkey shipped as the redis package in Ubuntu 26.04) as a low-latency feature cache, Aerospike for sub-ms feature serving (PayPal, Barclays, Forter migrations from Redis+Couchbase publicly cited), Apache Cassandra / ScyllaDB for historical state, plus ML feature stores Tecton (acquired by Databricks Aug 2025 at $900M, deeply integrated as 'Databricks Feature Store with Tecton'), Fennel (acquired by Databricks Apr 2025), Feast, Hopsworks, Chalk, and the new Redis Feature Form (Featureform acquired Oct 2025, formal product launch Apr 2026). The dominant production pattern at banks today is 'Kafka + Flink + Redis-or-Aerospike + scoring engine + case-management UI', and the regulator is comfortable with it because it has audit precedent. (b) Open-source AML-specific decision engines that overlap beava's territory at the feature+rule layer: Jube (AGPL-3.0, in-memory state for sub-ms decisioning, explicit AML+fraud positioning) and Marble / Checkmarble (open-source core with SaaS option, On-Prem deployable, positioned as 'flexible alternative to ComplyAdvantage / Actimize / Fiserv'). (c) The closed-loop AML platforms themselves (see competitive_incumbent_per_domain). Beava does NOT compete with layer (c) - those are buyers or embedding partners. Beava competes at layer (a) by collapsing the Kafka+Flink+Redis-or-Aerospike substrate into a single binary, with a secondary overlap with layer (b) at the rule-author level although beava ships no rules engine of its own.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: The AML-platform incumbents that buyers procure as black boxes - beava is NOT competing with these directly, it is the feature-substrate underneath that they (and in-house bank builds) are internally built on. Funding/scale as of 2025-2026: NICE Actimize - Nasdaq-owned, recognized as a Leader in Forrester Wave Q2 2025, 280+ predefined AML rules, FIS/Actimize/Fiserv/Experian/ACI top-5 holding ~40% market share in 2025 per industry trackers; Oracle FCCM; SAS Institute - top-5 AML market leader per industry forecasts (5.98B market 2025-2029); FICO TONBELLER Siron; IBM Safer Payments / Financial Crimes Insight; BAE Systems NetReveal; Verafin (Nasdaq) - dominant in US community-bank segment, explicit mule-detection product; SymphonyAI Sensa-NetReveal - launched Sensa Risk Intelligence Nov 2025 (AI-native, modular, 'go-live first use case in <3 months' positioning, 200 of top financial institutions, 2,000 enterprise customers); Hawk AI - $56M Series C Apr 2025 (One Peak lead, Macquarie/Rabobank/BlackFin/Sands/DN/Picus/Coalition participation), 80+ customers globally including Tier-1 banks, '150 ms average response, 70% false-positive reduction' positioning, FRAML platform, AI Overlay layered onto incumbent systems; ComplyAdvantage Mesh - launched Oct 2025 (AI-native, agentic, '82% fewer false positives', $0.29/entity/month blended mid-market pricing, ComplyLaunch 12-month free for early-stage fintechs); Flagright - $4.3M seed Apr 2025 (Frontline Ventures lead, YC alum), sub-300ms screening, no-code platform, AI-native; Lucinity - gen-AI case manager 'Luci'; Unit21 - $92M total funding, agentic AI platform; Sardine.ai - $70M Series C Feb 2025 (Activant Capital lead, a16z/Nyca/GV/Moody's/Experian Ventures), $145M total, FRAML convergence pitch, 2.2B devices profiled; Napier AI; Tookitaki; Castellum.AI; Salv; AMLYZE; Quantexa - $175M Series F Mar 2025 at $2.6B valuation (Teachers' Venture Growth lead), graph/entity-resolution 99% match accuracy, Q Assist AI, HSBC/Standard Chartered/BNY Mellon public references; Linkurious, TigerGraph, Neo4j for graph. Crypto-specific: Chainalysis (KYT/Reactor/Storyline, 1,500+ org clients, 9 of top-10 exchanges, FedRAMP); TRM Labs (FedRAMP High Dec 2024, $1B valuation, 77 chains, sub-second cross-chain); Elliptic (99% blockchain coverage, 100B+ data points, 2B+ labeled addresses); Solidus Labs, Nominis, Scorechain. M&A trend: Visa-Featurespace closed 2024 (rebranded 'ARIC Risk Hub' powered-by-Visa, A2A Protect launched 2025 covering push payments, request-to-pay, QR-based transfers, wallets) confirms scheme/network rollup, parallel to Equifax-Kount and Mastercard's risk-rollup pattern from the fraud segment.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Mixed but proprietary-dominant. The Tier-1 AML platform incumbents (NICE Actimize, SAS, Oracle FCCM, FICO, IBM, Verafin, SymphonyAI, ComplyAdvantage Mesh, Hawk, Flagright, Lucinity, Unit21, Sardine, Napier, Quantexa, Featurespace/Visa) are all closed-source proprietary SaaS or on-prem licensed. The feature-substrate layer beava actually competes at is mixed: Apache Flink (Apache-2.0), Kafka (Apache-2.0), Valkey (BSD-3-Clause, replacing Redis in Ubuntu 26.04 and most cloud-default deployments after the Redis-Valkey split resolved in Valkey's favor), Aerospike (proprietary Enterprise + Apache-2.0 community edition), Redis (post-AGPLv3/SSPL relicense, with Redis Feature Form sitting on top of Featureform's Mozilla 2.0/Apache stack post-acquisition), Tecton (now Databricks proprietary), Feast (Apache-2.0). Open-source AML-specific overlaps: Jube is AGPL-3.0 (a known dealbreaker for most bank legal teams), Marble is open-source core with commercial SaaS. Beava's Apache-2.0 with no open-core split is therefore a genuine and unusual posture in this segment - one of the very few Apache-2.0 options at the feature-substrate layer that also speaks AML primitives, and a clean alternative for buyers who reject AGPL (Jube) and BSL/proprietary (most of the rest). License posture is a hard buyer filter for AML-platform vendors who would embed beava across many bank tenants (they cannot ship AGPL into a closed-source product).
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: Medium and rising, but lower than for fraud (V1) and account abuse (V3). AML's regulator-mandated 5-7 year retention, FFIEC examination expectations, SR 11-7 / SR 26-02 model-validation pipeline, and multi-year procurement cycles materially blunt the hyperscaler-bundle threat in two ways: (1) tier-1 banks will not migrate AML stacks to a hyperscaler-native bundle without a 2-3 year procurement and model-validation cycle, and (2) data-residency requirements under EU AMLR / GDPR / MAS / FINTRAC push EU data on-EU and complicate any 'just run it on the hyperscaler' default. That said, three bundling vectors are real: (a) Databricks + Tecton (acquired Aug 2025) + Fennel (acquired Apr 2025) now offer a 'real-time feature store for fraud/risk/AML' in-platform - explicitly marketed for fraud detection and risk scoring as the first named use case, which collapses the feature-substrate layer beava plays in for any bank already running Databricks (which is many tier-2/tier-3 banks); (b) Redis Feature Form (Featureform-acquired-Oct-2025, launched Apr 2026) wraps the same shape for Redis-shop buyers; (c) Snowflake + Snowpark + dynamic tables increasingly host AML feature pipelines for warehouses-first banks. None of these can serve sub-ms TCP feature reads at beava's level today (Databricks/Tecton claims 0.8ms, Redis is the latency target), so beava still has a latency wedge - but the bundling threat is that the buyer no longer needs to procure a feature store separately, which removes beava from the consideration set even before latency is benchmarked. Crucially, NO hyperscaler ships an actual AML-rule library, case management, or SAR-filing connector bundled - those remain the closed-loop incumbents' moat - so beava's feature-substrate wedge is partially insulated even where the hyperscaler bundling lands.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Heavily Kafka-shaped and bank-specific - the worst-fit segment for beava's HTTP/TCP-push model so far. Bank-side producers: Kafka (overwhelmingly dominant at tier-1/tier-2 banks for the payment-event firehose), IBM MQ (legacy core-banking buses), vendor-specific buses (Tata BaNCS, Temenos T24, FIS IBS, Finastra), FedLine / FedNow API, SWIFT MX / pacs.008 / pacs.002, EBA RT1 / TIPS, NPCI UPI Switch, core-banking CDC (Goldengate, Debezium). EMI / neobank producers: Kafka, REST, Temporal. Crypto-exchange producers: in-house tx-firehose, Chainalysis KYT webhooks, TRM Labs API push, Elliptic Holistic API. Almost every existing AML feature store is Kafka-consumer-shaped (Tecton/Feast/Hopsworks/Fennel), while beava is HTTP/JSON :8080 + framed-TCP :8081 push-shaped - this is unusual in the AML stack. The natural beava integrations are: (a) a thin Kafka-to-beava-TCP sidecar (a few hundred lines of Rust or Python), or (b) direct ingestion from the payment-orchestration / core-banking event bus when that bus speaks HTTP (REST is increasingly common at modern neobanks and EMIs and at the crypto-exchange tier). gRPC support would close a recognised gap with Tecton/Chalk and help banks that standardise on gRPC internally. Outbound to the AML-platform rules / case-management UI is via batch_get HTTP, which is well-fit because AML case-investigator dashboards re-fetch features 20-100 times per case and HTTP/JSON is the lingua franca. Note that crypto exchanges and modern neobanks are materially more HTTP/REST-native than tier-1 banks - the beava integration story is much easier there.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, and the AML stack is more rules-engine-coupled than fraud is. Production AML stacks always run rules-and-ML in parallel: rule engines (Drools, OpenRules, FEEL, vendor DSLs inside Actimize/Hawk/Flagright/Napier/SymphonyAI Sensa) authored by MLROs and financial-crime analysts on top of features, and ML scorers (XGBoost, LightGBM, ONNX, isolation-forest, graph neural nets via Quantexa, transformer-based sequence models emerging) on the same features. Beava sits below both as the feature substrate and ships no rules engine of its own. Note that AML buyers expect the rules engine and case-management UI to be regulator-validated (SR 11-7 / SR 26-02, EBA model-validation guidelines, EU AMLR explainability requirements) - beava being feature-serving-only is a feature here, not a bug, because it keeps beava out of the regulator's model-validation perimeter and squarely in the 'derived data substrate' perimeter, which is a much smaller audit surface.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Five concrete reasons a buyer in this segment - specifically an AML-engineering or financial-crime-engineering team at a tier-2/tier-3 bank, EMI, neobank, money-transmitter, or crypto exchange building in-house or sidecarring an existing AML platform - would pick beava over the alternatives, framed honestly given AML is NOT a primary fit for beava: (1) Real-time TM enrichment layer - beava sits BESIDE the incumbent AML platform (Actimize / Hawk / ComplyAdvantage Mesh / Flagright / SymphonyAI Sensa) and pre-aggregates entity velocity features (1d/7d/30d transaction counts, distinct-counterparty cardinality via HLL, fan-in/fan-out, amount z-scores via t-digest, dormant-wake flags, country-corridor sums) that the rules engine and ML scorer fetch via batch_get before scoring - this 'feature pre-aggregation sidecar' positioning is the one beava can genuinely defend, NOT 'beava replaces your AML platform'. (2) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives covering counters, velocities, distinct-counts, distributions, ratios - the exact features AML teams hand-code as Flink streaming aggregations or Redis Lua scripts today, with structuring (count below threshold), peer-group z-scores, and dormant-wake all expressible as 1-2 line @bv.event declarations rather than 100+ line Flink jobs. (3) Single binary collapses the (Kafka+Flink+Redis-or-Aerospike+feature-store ETL) stack into one process for the AML feature-substrate layer; tier-2/tier-3 banks and crypto exchanges who lack the SRE depth to operate Flink+Kafka+Redis in production are an explicit segment. (4) Apache-2.0 with no open-core split and no acquisition risk is a genuine wedge against AGPL (Jube, which most bank legal teams reject), against the post-relicense Redis posture, against BSL/proprietary feature stores (Tecton-now-Databricks, Hopsworks Enterprise), and especially for AML-platform vendors who want to EMBED a feature substrate across many bank tenants and cannot ship AGPL inside a closed-source product. (5) Sub-millisecond TCP batch_get is far inside the AML latency budget (50-500ms typical, even 10s for EU IPR instant payment sanctions screening) - latency is NOT a wedge here (unlike V1 fraud), but it removes latency as a procurement objection and means beava is never the bottleneck in the 30-200 feature reads per AML decision plus investigator case-review re-fetch amplification.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete gaps blocking AML deployment today (derived from use case 8's open_engineering_gaps and SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md v0 invariants) - these are MORE numerous and MORE blocking than for fraud (V1), because AML is regulator-grade where fraud is liability-grade: (1) No TLS in v0 - non-negotiable dealbreaker for any regulated AML buyer; even with an mTLS-terminating proxy in front, MLROs and bank security teams want mTLS to the feature store itself, and 'plain TCP on a private subnet' is not auditable. (2) No authn/authz / RBAC - every regulated buyer needs per-tenant tokens, per-role access (Level-1 investigator vs MLRO vs auditor), and per-team audit; the absence of this is also a multi-tenancy blocker for AML-platform vendors. (3) No per-read audit log (who-asked-what-when) - directly required for AML reproducibility under FFIEC examination and EU AMLR explainability; this is the single most AML-specific gap. (4) No native point-in-time / as-of feature reads - 'what was structuring_count_30d for customer X at 14:32:07Z on 2026-02-14?' is a question regulators will ask and the answer must be reproducible; beava's in-memory state and WAL-only durability cannot answer it today. (5) No hot-standby / synchronous-WAL replication - losing 90-365 days of behavioural baseline on a node crash, even with WAL replay, is unacceptable to most MLRO teams; AML state lifecycles are months-to-years where fraud is hours-to-days, so the cost of a state-loss event is materially higher. (6) No in-process sharding - caps single-tenant scale at one node; the long AML state-lifecycle (90-365 day baselines + dormant-wake to 180-365 days) pushes state size beyond comfortable single-node RAM for tier-1 buyers and large crypto exchanges (100M-1B+ entity cardinality). (7) In-memory only / no tiered storage - 90-365 day lookbacks push state size beyond single-node RAM; tiered RAM-to-SSD is needed and absent. (8) No native idempotency tokens on push (dedupe by transaction_id / end_to_end_id / tx_hash) - at-least-once upstream Kafka/Kinesis rails will double-count CTR aggregates and structuring counters without it, and the regulator-exact thresholds ($10k CTR, structuring just-below-threshold) cannot tolerate that. (9) No triggers / no webhook on threshold-cross - AML teams want 'emit STRUCTURING_ALERT when count(deposits<$10k in 30d)>=N AND sum_below_threshold_ratio>p' fired by the feature store; today the buyer must poll. (10) No multi-tenancy / no namespace ACLs - AML-platform vendors wanting to embed beava across many bank customers need either per-tenant binaries (operationally painful) or namespace + sharding (not in v0). (11) No native sanctions / PEP / adverse-media list lookup hook - every competitor ships this and AML rules engines expect it at the feature-substrate layer or right next to it. (12) No graph / entity-resolution layer - Quantexa, Linkurious, TigerGraph, Neo4j own mule-ring discovery; beava cannot enter this conversation. (13) No case-management UI / no SAR-narrative generator - Lucinity / Unit21 / Sardine / Verafin / NICE Actimize / Hawk own this entire workflow; beava does not and should not compete here. (14) No deterministic-replay-from-WAL with verifiable hashes - regulators want to recompute alerts from raw events with a hash chain; the current WAL is crash-safe but not regulator-audit-grade. (15) No data-residency controls (EU-only RAM, US-only RAM) for GDPR / EU AMLR / MAS / FINTRAC. (16) No GDPR right-to-erasure surface that does not corrupt aggregate counters - non-trivial design issue. (17) No Kafka source/sink connector - the dominant AML producer is Kafka, and the absence of a first-class connector means every adopter writes the same sidecar. (18) No multi-year retention story - the 5-7 year supporting-documentation retention bar is satisfied by archiving upstream events + decision log to cold storage, but beava ships no documented pattern for this and the buyer must design it themselves.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 12mo+ for any tier-1 bank, 6-12mo for a tier-2/tier-3 bank or crypto exchange design partner, 3-6mo for an AML-platform vendor who would EMBED beava as a feature substrate behind their own UI. The first-tier procurement-non-starter gaps (TLS+authn+RBAC+per-read audit log+idempotency tokens, items 1+2+3+8 above) are roughly 2-3 months on their own. The AML-specific differentiating gaps (point-in-time reads item 4, hot-standby/replication item 5, triggers item 9, deterministic-replay-with-hash item 14, Kafka connector item 17, multi-year retention pattern item 18) are another 3-6 months. The tier-1-scale gaps (in-process sharding item 6, tiered storage item 7, multi-tenancy item 10, data-residency item 15, GDPR erasure item 16) are 6-12+ months and are blockers for the largest global banks - not required for first design partners. Note: even with all of the above, AML procurement cycles at tier-1 banks are structurally 18-36 months and require model validation under SR 26-02 / EBA, MLRO sign-off, SOC2 / ISO 27001, and independent testing per FFIEC - the engineering-time figure understates the calendar-time-to-revenue. The AML-platform-vendor-embed path (3-6 months engineering) bypasses most of the procurement cycle because the bank is already procuring the AML-platform vendor's product - beava is invisible substrate underneath.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Zero external proof points and zero repo evidence for AML specifically. Beava-side: no publicly named users in AML/transaction monitoring, no published case study, no conference talks, no @ACAMS / FinCrime Central / AMLintelligence presence, no GitHub Discussion / RFC threads on AML transaction monitoring located in the use case 8 deep research. Repo evidence is materially weaker than for fraud (V1): no AML-vertical demo at the searched paths in python/beava/demos, no AML-shaped workload in crates/beava-bench/, no AML-shaped acceptance test in python/tests/v0. The python/beava/_demo.py and demo data loaders exist but are not AML-vertical. Competitor-side validation that the segment shape is real: Quantexa public references at HSBC / Standard Chartered / BNY Mellon, Hawk monitors billions of transactions across European and US banks with 80+ customers including Tier-1, Featurespace/Visa at HSBC / NatWest / Worldpay processing 100B payments/year pre-A2A-Protect, Feedzai at Citi / Standard Chartered / Lloyds ($75M raise Oct 2025 at $2B valuation, framework agreement with ECB for digital euro fraud detection), Verafin used by thousands of US community banks via Nasdaq, Chainalysis serving 9 of top-10 crypto exchanges, Elliptic 2M+ screenings/month, TRM Labs 77+ chains at FedRAMP High, ComplyAdvantage Mesh '82% fewer false positives' Oct 2025 launch, SymphonyAI Sensa Risk Intelligence Nov 2025 launch claiming '<3 month first-use-case go-live'. Buyer pain is well-documented (industry-wide 85-95% false-positive rates per Everest Group, $940M US AML enforcement penalties in 2025 per Wolters Kluwer, AMLA Work Programme 2025 publishing 23 Level-2/Level-3 technical standards by 10 July 2026, EU IPR mandatory acceptance Jan 2025 and mandatory sending Oct 2025 forcing <10s SEPA Instant sanctions screening). Beava knows roughly who the buyer is (AML-platform vendor wanting to embed a feature substrate, or a tier-2/tier-3 bank or crypto exchange building in-house) but has zero published proof points and zero repo evidence to that buyer.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Watch - AML is a poor primary fit for beava in v0 and pursuing tier-1 banks directly would be a 12-24 month engineering and procurement timeline against entrenched incumbents (NICE Actimize, SAS, Oracle FCCM) with multi-decade audit precedent and a regulator-comfortable Kafka+Flink+Redis status quo. The two viable narrow paths are: (a) an embed deal with one AML-platform vendor (Hawk, ComplyAdvantage Mesh, Flagright, SymphonyAI Sensa, Marble) where beava is invisible feature substrate underneath, 3-6 months of engineering on TLS+authn+per-read-audit-log+idempotency+Kafka-connector, and the bank-side procurement cycle is the vendor's problem not beava's; (b) a tier-2/tier-3 crypto exchange or neobank building in-house (HTTP/REST-native, less Kafka-dependent, more open-source-friendly, faster procurement than tier-1 banks), 6-12 months including point-in-time reads and hot-standby. Do NOT pitch beava as a NICE Actimize / SAS / Oracle FCCM replacement - that is a different sale, different buyer (MLRO + Head of FinCrime, not engineering), regulator-validated black box, and beava cannot ship the rules library or case-management UI or SAR-filing connector that defines that procurement. Pitch beava as 'real-time TM enrichment layer that pre-aggregates entity velocity features before they hit the rules engine' and let the incumbent AML platform keep the regulator-facing surface. The EU AMLA/AMLR 2027 application and EU IPR 2025 instant-payment AML mandate are real urgency drivers, but they push buyers toward established RegTech vendors first; beava can only ride that wave as a substrate, not as the regulator-facing product.
